context_requirements: Active Wnt/β-catenin signaling, ideally with APC or CTNNB1 mutation or other Wnt pathway activation
Expression of tankyrase substrates such as AXIN1/2 and angiomotins
YAP/TAZ activity for the angiomotin-mediated YAP-suppressive arm
Intact or permissive cell-cycle machinery for G1 arrest and senescence responses
falsifiers: No decrease in MYC, CCND1, CCND3, CCNE2, MYBL2, E2F2, TFDP1, PCNA, MCM3, TOP2A, BIRC5, AURKA, PLK1, UBE2C or CDC20 at 24 h in HT29 or other APC-mutant lines
No increase in AXIN1, TLE1, TCFL5, DUSP4, DUSP6, SPRY2, SPRED2, RGS2, IER3, ZFP36, FOSL1, EGR1 or BHLHE40 at 6 h or 24 h
No G1 arrest or proliferation-down signature at 24 h in responsive lines
Strong and equal transcriptional responses in all nine lines, including Wnt-inactive lines, indistinguishable from generic cytotoxicity
Clear response at 6 h that is not sustained or amplified at 24 h

evidence.supports: IWR-1 tankyrase inhibitor attenuates Wnt/β-catenin signaling and downstream target gene expression in cancer stem-like cells
RK-287107 tankyrase inhibitor causes Axin2 accumulation and downregulates β-catenin and TCF/LEF target gene expression in APC-mutated colorectal cancer cells
Tankyrase inhibition stabilizes angiomotins, suppresses YAP activity and YAP target gene expression, and sensitizes lung cancer cells to EGFR inhibition
MSC2504877 tankyrase inhibitor suppresses Wnt/β-catenin signaling, enhances G1 arrest and senescence, and suppresses Cyclin D2 and Cyclin E2
XAV-939 tankyrase inhibitor alters global gene expression and enhances osteoblastogenesis in human mesenchymal stem cells
